{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"0a050f8874de92f4dc9e173cd12f4179f21547e7533379fa998954c338cbe5b2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:28","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving situations: roundabouts, metered ramps, diverging diamond interchanges, traffic stops, deer and funeral processions","heading":"C — Driving situations: entering, driving and exiting one-lane and two-lane roundabouts, ramp meters, diverging diamond interchanges, what to do at a traffic stop, avoiding and reporting deer crashes, and funeral processions","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driving situations: entering, driving and exiting one-lane and two-lane roundabouts, ramp meters, diverging diamond interchanges, what to do at a traffic stop, avoiding and reporting deer crashes, and funeral processions
Knowledge domain: special situations a new Wisconsin driver meets — roundabout yielding and lane choice, freeway ramp signals, diverging diamond interchanges, behaving safely when stopped by police, deer hazards and funeral processions.

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
The handbook presents roundabouts as a safer and more efficient way to move traffic, and traffic inside one always circulates counterclockwise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Overhead signs on the approach show which lane to use; generally the left lane is for left turns, the right lane for the next right, and the middle lane for going straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
As you approach a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicycles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
Before entering, yield to traffic coming from your left that is already in the roundabout, and yield to semitrucks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Enter only when there is a safe gap, and if the roundabout is empty you do not have to wait. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
Inside the roundabout keep your speed low, stay in your lane and never switch lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
When you near your exit, turn on your right turn signal and leave the roundabout. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
If an emergency vehicle with its siren on enters a roundabout before you do, pull over and let it go by instead of entering. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
If you are already in the roundabout when an emergency vehicle comes, leave at the next right exit and then pull over, avoiding any stop inside the circle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
At a one-lane roundabout a bicyclist may either ride through the roundabout or use the crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians crossing at a roundabout look left for oncoming traffic from the curb and look right once they reach the crosswalk island. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A03
At a two-lane roundabout your lane choice is critical: choose a lane and yield to traffic in both lanes before you enter. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A03
In a two-lane roundabout, use the left lane for left turns and U-turns, the right lane for right turns, and follow the pavement markings, arrows or signs to go straight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A03
A bicyclist at a two-lane roundabout may take the travel lane through it or leave the roadway and use the crosswalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A03
Some freeway on-ramps have traffic signals that space out merging vehicles, which eases congestion on both the freeway and the ramp. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A03
A ramp is being metered when its Ramp Metered When Flashing sign is lit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A03
At a metered ramp, pull all the way up to the white stop line so your tires set off the sensors in the pavement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A03
Each ramp lane has its own signal, and you may go and merge into traffic once your signal turns green. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A03
Disobeying a ramp meter signal can earn you a ticket. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A04
A diverging diamond interchange routes drivers smoothly through exits and entrances to improve safety, reduce crowding and cut road costs; follow its signs, signals and markings. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A04
Wisconsin lists four diverging diamond interchanges: I-39/90 at WIS 11/Avalon Road south of Janesville, WIS 441 at Oneida Street in Appleton, I-39/90 at WIS 26/Milton Avenue in Janesville, and I-39/90 at WIS 81 in Beloit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A04
Law enforcement's top priority is public safety, and during a stop the officer checks for a possible incident, crime or minor law violation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A04
When you see emergency lights flashing behind you, pull off to the right side of the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A05
Once stopped, shift into park and turn off both the engine and the radio. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A05
During a traffic stop, stay inside the vehicle with your seat belt fastened and roll your window down. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A05
Keep your hands on top of the steering wheel where the officer can see them, and avoid sudden moves or reaching for things. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A05
Do not argue if you get a ticket; you will have a chance to raise your concerns before a judge or court. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A05
Deer are most active between sunset and sunrise. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A05
Scan for your headlights reflecting in a deer's eyes; if you see them, slow down, sound your horn and be ready to stop. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A05
Expect more than one deer, and remember they wander from rural areas into towns and cities and can cross at any place and time. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A05
After hitting a deer, first check that your vehicle is still safe to drive, then record the time, place and details for insurance and crash reports. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A05
A driver who hits a deer may keep it, and if that driver does not want it, the next motorist may keep it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A05
Call the police after hitting a deer so they can issue a tag for it, and call them to say where it is if you do not want the deer. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A05
A funeral procession carries the deceased from a funeral home or place of worship to a cemetery or crematorium. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A05
The first vehicle in a funeral procession must obey traffic signs and signals, and every vehicle in the line must have its headlights on. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A05
Never cut into a funeral procession or interfere with it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

Misconceptions: you do not stop and wait at an empty roundabout; you never change lanes inside a roundabout; when an emergency vehicle comes you do not stop inside the circle but exit first; at a ramp meter you pull all the way to the white line, not short of it, so the pavement sensors detect you; the roadside is not the place to argue a ticket; seeing one deer does not mean the danger has passed.
Mnemonics: slow, yield left, find a gap, stay in lane, signal right to leave; at a stop think park, off, belt on, window down, hands up top; deer eyes glow, so slow, honk and be ready to stop.
Glossary: roundabout means a circular intersection where traffic flows counterclockwise around a center island; ramp meter means a signal on a freeway entrance ramp that spaces out vehicles merging onto the freeway; diverging diamond interchange means an interchange that guides traffic through crossing exit and entrance paths; funeral procession means a line of vehicles traveling with the deceased.
Dynamic facts: the list of diverging diamond interchanges in Wisconsin can grow as new ones are built, so the named locations reflect this handbook edition.
